title: Studio Access pillar: the field-permission editor shows a different edit right for a field with no explicit rule than the runtime enforces, and its bulk controls change edit rights silently (detail withheld pending maintainer)
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect, reproduced and confirmed in code, landing site named (maintainer direct dispatch, authorizing words quoted in the audit comment).

## Symptom (customer-visible)

In Studio › Access › a permission set › an object's field sub-table, the readable/editable state shown for a field that has **no explicit field rule** disagrees with what the server enforces for that same field. An admin who trusts the screen gets the opposite of what they see.

The bulk/clear controls in that sub-table look like no-ops on screen, but they write explicit field rules that change who can edit.

- This is an authorization-display defect, so the step-by-step reproduction and the exact direction of the mismatch are withheld from this card, per the maintainer's instruction. They go to the implementer privately.

## Measured

- Repo `3fcafcd3`, 2026-10-27, by the Studio QA Access card. The member's write was refused or accepted against what the editor displayed.
- The coordinator confirmed the mismatch by reading the editor's render default against the server's field-masking rule for unruled fields.

## Landing site (suspected — the implementer verifies)

- Editor side: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` (field sub-table render default and the field-permission seed on update).
- Runtime side: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts`.
- Which side is wrong is decided by the spec's declared meaning of an absent field rule (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`). Per the protocol-first rule, code aligns to the spec; changing the spec is a separate card.

## Acceptance

- For every combination of object grant × field rule (absent / readable-only / editable), the editor shows exactly what the runtime enforces.
- No bulk or clear control writes an edit right the admin did not see change on screen.
- A pin covers the absent-rule case on both sides (editor render and runtime enforcement), so they cannot drift again.

## Filing facts

- Business reason: admins decide who may change sensitive fields from this screen. A display that disagrees with enforcement either leaves a field editable that the admin believes is locked, or locks one they meant to keep open, with no signal either way.
- Reader who acts: an `os-dev` implementer, dispatched directly by this PM session on the maintainer's instruction (`domain:ui`).
- Dedupe: semantic search `permission set field permission editor default editable display runtime field-masker unruled field` on objectstack-ai/objectstack → 3 hits (#22379, #21063, #9127), all closed and none about this editor/runtime mismatch.
- Source: Studio QA run, 2026-10-27, coordinator session `session_01J8VVAkZns5rNnK2rtszzbQ`.
